column1: # Each committed tests/golden/*.bpf.c compiled with the production clang
# flags and loaded with tools/spnl_load_check.c. Only the STATUS column is
# compared; `note` is prose for the reviewer (the compiler/verifier message
# itself is version-dependent and deliberately not pinned — see the header
# A non-ok status is not permission to leave it broken: it is a claim that
# somebody looked. Refresh with `sh tools/golden_compile.sh --update` and
# review the diff — a new failure means the codegen started emitting C that
# does not build or does not load.

column3: recursion: fib calls itself and the verifier refuses BPF-to-BPF recursion ("recursive call from fib_inner() to fib_inner()"). Inherent to eBPF, not kernel-specific. E405 verdict: wrong LAYER (a partition/validate check could name it), not a wrong program; detecting it statically is a named follow-up, not done here.

signed division (`@b * @h / 2`): the BPF ISA has no signed div before v4 and the CLI pins -mcpu=v1 (E403). Measured OK at -mcpu=v4 (E403 s2 matrix). Legal Ruby; the DSL workaround is divu (E086). E405 verdict: real ISA constraint, loud but diagnosed by clang rather than by us.
E392: `param :x, default: N` -> volatile const __s64 in .rodata. Loads clean; the point of the golden is that the declaration produces a real, patchable global rather than a folded literal.

E399: `filter_by :pid, :comm` -> volatile const .rodata + spnl_filter_discard(), injected into both entry wrappers. Loads clean with every key unset, which is the case that has to work: the verifier folds the guards (and the bpf_get_current_* calls inside them) out of the accepted program.

E399: all six filter keys plus the uid/gid builtins. Pins the maximal spnl_filter_discard() (paired helper calls for pid/tid and uid/gid) and proves the 16-byte comm compare unrolls within the instruction budget.

E394: emit_kfield_str on both shapes a string field can have (dentry->d_name.name is a pointer, super_block->s_id is a char[32] three hops in) from ONE source form. That it loads is the point: the shape is chosen by the C type system, not by the author.

E394: kfield_str_eq driving an `if` in a kprobe (where bpf_d_path is structurally impossible, E390 c65) and a deny in fmod_ret. The 15-char literal compiles to a 24-byte buffer and a `ret == 16` guard — one spare byte, because probe_read_kernel_str truncates silently (E394 D3).

negative fixture (E394): kfield_str_eq written without its compare literal, so the field path silently loses its last hop and ends on `struct dentry *`. SPNL_KSTR_CHECK refuses it and names this Ruby call. If this ever turns `ok`, the D2 shape check has been weakened and reading a struct pointer as a string is back.

kernel kfunc filter, not us: bpf_qdisc_init_prologue is refused with -EACCES on 7.1.5-ebpf. Measured (E405, results/E405/s2_qdisc_prologue.txt): hand-written C calling it DIRECTLY from the SEC("struct_ops/init") entry is refused identically, bpf_qdisc_reset_destroy_epilogue is refused the same way, and the same qdisc with both kfuncs dropped is LOAD_OK. Extends E095. May differ on another kernel.
